title: Local KMS / Escrow & Vault Connector Review with Titan Financial
summary: Deep dive on integrating Redwood with Titan's local KMS/HSM and escrow process; discussed envelope encryption, key wrapping, audit logs, rotation cadence, SOC2 evidence, and cert pinning for the Vault connector. Agreed to run a short bench test and exchange SOC2 artifact and HSM onboarding guide.
topics: encryption at rest and in transit
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC 2 Type II report and HSM onboarding checklist
Titan to provision test HSM credentials and certs for bench run
Schedule a 90-min bench test w/ SE + Titan Cloud Eng next week
Share proposed rotation cadence and escrow SLA draft
action_items: Maya Chen | Send SOC2 report, HSM onboarding checklist, and Vault connector spec | 2026-04-09
Liam O'Connor | Prepare bench test script (envelope encryption, live rotate) | 2026-04-12
Andre Souza | Provision test HSM instance, export connection certs | 2026-04-10
Priya Malhotra | Confirm data residency requirement with legal (EU-only) | 2026-04-13
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-07 15:00 PT | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE); Rachel Lee (Titan Security Lead); Andre Souza (Cloud Engineer); Priya Malhotra (Compliance)

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Liam's our solutions engineer. we set aside 50 minutes to walk through the vault / local KMS integration and the escrow approach you mentioned.
00:18 Rachel Lee: Thanks Maya. we wanted to make sure we cover two things: one, how Redwood will use our HSM/BYOK for at-rest keys and second, how audit logs and retention line up with our SOC2/ISO controls.
00:30 Liam O'Connor: perfect. high-level first: Redwood supports envelope encryption for model artifacts and customer data at rest. you host the root key in your HSM (BYOK) — we do key wrapping with a local intermediate, and the wrapped keys live in our control plane only as opaque blobs. that keeps your master key in your custody.
00:52 Andre Souza: quick clarification — when you say "wrapped keys live in control plane as opaque blobs", are those stored encrypted at rest in Redwood? and can we see the audit events for unwrap/wrap operations?
01:06 Liam O'Connor: yes, they remain encrypted at rest. we will emit audit events for wrap/unwrap calls, key usage, and admin operations. there are two event streams — system-level and tenant-level; you can push sys-level events to your SIEM via syslog or secure push. sometimes the auto transcript mislabels sys-level but it's really distinct streams.
01:24 Priya Malhotra: and the logs include the key ID and operation, not the plaintext?
01:30 Liam O'Connor: correct, only key IDs and request metadata. we never log plaintext keys, obviously. we also support configurable retention to meet your policy (we can keep for 1, 3, 7 years — depends on plan and your legal needs).
01:45 Rachel Lee: on the HSM side — we're using a Thales Luna solution on-prem and our compliance team wants an HSM-backed import or escrow flow. we don't want Redwood to ever have unwrapped key material.
02:00 Maya Chen: understood. our BYOK flow supports two patterns: key import where you generate keys in your HSM and never export them, and an escrow model where you escrow wrapped key blobs with a secondary KMS that you control. which are you leaning toward?
02:17 Andre Souza: ideally the generate-in-HSM-then-never-export approach, but for key recovery we need an escrow policy. the escrow must be under our legal control and have multi-sig access.
02:30 Liam O'Connor: that's doable. for recovery we suggest using a split-key escrow in your vault cluster — essentially you store recovery shares in two separate vault nodes or in a second provider. Redwood's connector will only hold a sealed, wrapped version and require your approval for recovery actions. the manual recovery path triggers an audit event and an approval webhook to the tenant owners.
02:54 Rachel Lee: does Redwood support HSM attestation and remote attestation proofs so we can verify the key never left the HSM?
03:03 Liam O'Connor: yes, we can accept attestation tokens from your HSM (for supported vendors) and record them in the onboarding evidence. we also support cert chains for the HSM device; you'll push those during provisioning.
03:18 Priya Malhotra: okay, switching to in-transit — do you require mTLS between Redwood connectors and our vault? and is cert pinning an option?
03:28 Liam O'Connor: we support mTLS and cert pinning for the Vault connector. recommended is mTLS for mutual authentication plus cert pinning to avoid MITM if there's a proxy in the path. the connector will validate your server cert chain and present a client cert issued by your CA.
03:48 Andre Souza: great. network question: will the connector initiate outbound connections to Redwood, or does Redwood reach into our network? we prefer egress-only from our VPC for security reasons.
03:58 Maya Chen: recommended pattern is egress-only. the connector in your VPC initiates outbound TLS to Redwood control plane endpoints, using mTLS. for private deployments we can also run a customer-hosted control plane if you want zero outbound.
04:14 Rachel Lee: I thought private deployment had a different billing model — also curious about SLA differences.
04:21 Maya Chen: correct — Private (on-prem or VPC) is a separate contract and gives you full control; SLA is negotiable in enterprise contracts. Dedicated gives good isolation but still uses Redwood-managed control plane. We can go into commercial details after technical alignment.
04:36 Priya Malhotra: back to auditability — we need tamper-evident logs for key usage that align to our SOC 2 controls. can you produce signed audit logs or do we ingest raw events?
04:50 Liam O'Connor: we can export signed event batches using a signing key; the signatures are verifiable. alternative is streaming raw events to your SIEM via a secure push. whichever you prefer, both meet typical SOC2 evidence requirements.
05:06 Rachel Lee: what's the granularity — per-token or per-key? we need to show who invoked which key for which operation.
05:14 Liam O'Connor: per-operation metadata includes: key ID, operation (wrap/unwrap/sign), timestamp, caller identity (Redwood service principal + tenant id), and request origin IP. Not at per-token generation level though — tokens are opaque; but we can correlate request ids to higher-level operations.
05:32 Andre Souza: rotation — what cadence do you support and can you coordinate cross-tenant rotations without downtime?
05:40 Liam O'Connor: we support rolling rotations with zero-downtime for active sessions via dual-key validity periods. you can set rotation windows (e.g., 30/90/365 days), and Redwood will pre-rotate wrapped keys and keep both versions valid for a grace period. for master key rotates in HSM, we recommend rotating the intermediate every 6–12 months and master per your policy.
06:03 Priya Malhotra: are there constraints for model checkpoints or cached KV cache (the transcript earlier said K-V cache) and how those keys get rotated?
06:14 Liam O'Connor: good call — the KV cache for decoding uses ephemeral session keys derived from the wrapped keys; those session keys are rotated frequently and do not require re-wrapping. model checkpoints are encrypted with tenant-specific data keys which follow the same envelope pattern and will be re-encrypted during a key rotation process we automate.
06:36 Rachel Lee: any risk that rotating keys could cause corruption of artifacts or inability to decrypt older logs?
06:44 Liam O'Connor: we maintain key version history; during rotation we keep older key versions to allow decryption of legacy artifacts. we never delete previous wrapping keys until retention and legal policy allow.
06:57 Maya Chen: quick sidebar — a few customers ask about confidentiality for intermediate keys when using Redwood's hosted control plane. TLDR: the intermediate is created in a customer-owned enclave or generated by you and only wrapped by your master key. Redwood cannot unwrap without your HSM approvals.
07:15 Andre Souza: good. about escrow: can escrow shares be stored in a government-approved KMS for cross-border compliance? we have EU-restricted data and a requirement that escrow copies live in EU jurisdiction.
07:27 Liam O'Connor: yes, you can store escrow shares in an EU-only vault or another HSM in region. Redwood's connector supports region-specific endpoints and you can configure the escrow target per-tenant.
07:40 Priya Malhotra: for audit reasons we also need a runbook describing the recovery flow with required approvals. do you have a template?
07:48 Maya Chen: yes, we'll share our recovery runbook template. it includes the multi-sig steps, webhook triggers, and audit snapshots for each step. we'll mark the parts where you insert your internal approvers.
08:01 Rachel Lee: let's discuss certificate management for the connector. how are client certs rotated and how do we validate the connector certs?
08:10 Liam O'Connor: client certs can be rotated on your CA schedule. Redwood supports SCEP and ACME flows for automated cert rotation, or you can push certs manually via the onboarding API. the connector will present a client cert signed by your CA; Redwood will validate it against the pinned CA bundle.
08:26 Andre Souza: does Redwood support hardware-backed client certs on the connector side? we want the connector key material in a local TPM or HSM if possible.
08:35 Liam O'Connor: yes, the connector can leverage local TPM or HSM to protect client private keys. our installer supports configuring the connector to use PKCS#11 for private key operations. note that OS-level TPM support can vary by distro.
08:50 Priya Malhotra: compliance question: for SOC2/ISO evidence, besides signed logs and the SOC2 report, what artifacts can you provide?
08:59 Maya Chen: we can provide architecture diagrams, encryption topology (keys-at-rest and in-transit), access control matrix (RBAC), SSO/SAML configuration screenshots, and sample audit event exports. for ISO we can provide policy mappings as well.
09:15 Rachel Lee: SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. do you recommend SCIM for onboarding service accounts and grouping?
09:24 Liam O'Connor: yes, SCIM for identity provisioning is recommended. it lets you sync group membership for RBAC. for audit trails, we also capture SSO events (login, token exchange) in the tenant audit stream.
09:39 Andre Souza: small note — are there any features behind dedicated or private plans we would need for full HSM integration?
09:47 Maya Chen: the full customer-managed KMS/HSM pattern with zero export is typically part of Private deployments or an advanced Dedicated contract. Hosted can do BYOK and connector flows, but if you require zero outbound and fully private control plane we would go Private. we can detail options in the commercial doc.
10:01 Rachel Lee: understood. how about data residency — if our EU tenancy uses EU-only models and storage, can you pin compute and storage regions?
10:10 Liam O'Connor: yes, Redwood supports region pinning for model serving and storage. for Private deployments we can also host the entire control plane in your region. we usually keep a replication plan for DR but you can restrict cross-region replication.
10:24 Priya Malhotra: question on legal: will Redwood sign a key custody addendum that clarifies you won't access unwrapped keys and lays out escrow SLA?
10:33 Maya Chen: yes, we have a key custody addendum template we can share. it enumerates controls, proof of no-access, and escrow SLAs. we often include HSM vendor attestation language.
10:45 Rachel Lee: curious about the performance overhead — does using customer HSM for wrap/unwrap add latency to inference calls?
10:53 Liam O'Connor: we avoid calling HSM synchronously for every inference. we use short-lived session keys cached in the runtime; unwrap is performed during session establishment and then session keys are used locally. typical added latency for session establishment is a few hundred ms depending on HSM response. token-level inference is unaffected.
11:16 Andre Souza: that matches our expectation. for bench tests, we'd like to measure session establishment time and a small token loop.
11:24 Maya Chen: Liam will prepare a bench script for exactly that.
11:28 Liam O'Connor: yes, I'll include: HSM unwrap latency, 1k token loop, and a rotate-then-decrypt verification.
11:36 Rachel Lee: do you have knobs to throttle key usage or rate-limit unwraps to prevent cryptographic DoS?
11:44 Liam O'Connor: we expose rate limits on key operations per tenant and per key ID. we can also gate unwraps behind additional approvals for critical keys.
11:54 Priya Malhotra: let's talk about the connector lifecycle: upgrades, security patches, and patch evidence. we need a way to verify the connector binary hasn't been tampered with.
12:05 Maya Chen: the connector binaries are signed; we publish SHAs and GPG signatures. for Private deployments we can provide an SBOM and patch cadence. we also support automated update channels or locked versions for air-gapped installs.
12:22 Andre Souza: excellent. on the topic of attestations, earlier you mentioned device attestation — can you consume TPM quotes from our connector host?
12:32 Liam O'Connor: yes we can accept TPM quotes for attestation during onboarding, and we can store the quote in the onboarding evidence bundle. if you want periodic re-attestation, we can schedule that as well.
12:44 Rachel Lee: it sounds like the mechanics are there. a few edge concerns from compliance: inter-region key use, legal holds, and subpoena processes. how do you handle legal requests for keys?
12:58 Maya Chen: Redwood has a documented process — we don't have access to unwrapped keys and will notify the tenant and follow the escrow/legal procedures defined in the contract. any forced disclosure would be handled per jurisdictional law; we will include notification clauses where allowed. your legal team can review the template.
13:20 Priya Malhotra: please include those templates in the packet.
13:24 Maya Chen: will do.
13:27 Andre Souza: another nit: are backups for wrapped keys encrypted separately and are they also signed for integrity?
13:35 Liam O'Connor: yes backups are stored encrypted and signed; backup manifests include checksums and signatures to detect tamper. we can also provide root-of-trust statements for backup storage.
13:48 Rachel Lee: timeline-wise, we hope to have a short pilot in the next three weeks. does that fit your capacity?
13:56 Maya Chen: yes, if you can provision the test HSM creds this week we'll schedule the bench run next week and then a short pilot after.
14:03 Liam O'Connor: I'll send the bench script and a handshake checklist after the call.
14:09 Rachel Lee: one more question — are hardware escrow keys subject to the same retention and destruction controls? if we ask for key destruction after a contract ends can you prove deletion?
14:21 Liam O'Connor: yes, we support provable deletion for wrapped blobs and can provide deletion receipts. for HSM-resident master keys you control, you'd handle the HSM destruction; for anything Redwood holds we'll produce a cryptographic deletion proof and update audit logs.
14:39 Priya Malhotra: perfect. that addresses our concerns.
14:43 Maya Chen: recap of next steps: send SOC2 and HSM onboarding checklist, bench script, and schedule bench. agreed?
14:51 Rachel Lee: agreed.
14:53 Andre Souza: agreed.
14:54 Priya Malhotra: agreed.
15:00 Maya Chen: great. thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.

(remaining 37 minutes were Q&A and detailed technical clarifications; excerpted above to keep transcript focused on the main decisions and next steps)

End of transcript.
